_about: Credit-card tap-to-ride in Tokyo (and Osaka Metro). Every rule here was read on the operator's own page on the 'checked' date; anything an official page did not say is left out. Re-check before 2027-03-25 (one year after the 11-operator mutual use began) or sooner if JR East announces support.
title: Can You Tap a Credit Card at Tokyo Train Gates? JR vs Subway (2026)
description: Tokyo Metro, Toei and nine other Kanto railways take contactless cards at the gate. JR East does not. Where your card works, and what to do if you can't exit.
h1: Can you tap a credit card at Tokyo train gates?
lead: Short answer: yes on the subway, no on JR trains. Here is where a contactless card or phone works, why a gate might refuse it, and what to do if you can't get out.
quick: On the Tokyo subway (Tokyo Metro and Toei) and nine other Tokyo-area railways, you can tap a contactless credit or debit card, or your phone, at the gate.

On JR trains (JR East), you can't. That includes the Yamanote Line, the Chuo Line and the Narita Express. You can still buy a JR ticket with a credit card at a ticket office or a purple ticket machine.
Use the same card or phone to get in and out. The same card on your phone counts as a different card.
A JR Pass doesn't cover the Tokyo subway.
A Suica or PASMO card works on all of them, JR included.

stuck.title: Can't get out of the gate?
stuck.intro: Stop tapping other cards. The gate is looking for the trip you started.
steps: It's the gate next to the station office window. Or press the call button on the gate. Don't try other gates.
Show the card or phone you used to get in
Hold up the exact card or phone you tapped on the way in. A different card, or the same card on a different device, counts as a new trip.
Tell the staff which station you started from. They will tell you what to pay and how.
Did your train keep going onto a JR line?

Some subway trains keep running onto JR tracks without you changing trains. Tokyo Metro says your card trip then doesn't count at all, and you pay in two parts, in cash or another way that isn't a credit card: first at your exit, for the JR part of the ride; later, at a station of the railway you started on (a Tokyo Metro station if you started there), for the subway part. Bring the same card so staff can clear your trip.
Take the same card to a ticket window of the railway you started on. Tokyo Metro no longer hands out reception numbers (that ended October 25, 2026).
phrases: I got on at ___ station with this card. The gate won't open.
このカードで ___ 駅から乗りました。改札が開きません。
My train kept going onto the JR line.
電車がそのままJR線に乗り入れました。
どうやって精算すればいいですか？
I only have a credit card.
クレジットカードしか持っていません。
stuck.phrasesNote: Show the Japanese line to station staff. Say your station name in English; they will understand.

where.title: Where can I tap my credit card?
where.intro: Whether a card works depends on the railway company, not the station. Big stations like Shinjuku have gates from several companies next to each other, and only some of them take cards.

rows.name: Tokyo Metro
notes: If your train keeps going onto a JR East, Saitama Rapid Railway or Toyo Rapid Railway line, your card doesn't cover that part.
You can't start a card trip at Nakano. If you get off at Nakano, pay at the staffed window with the card you used.
Switching between Tokyo Metro and Toei on a card gets you ¥70 off, just like other tickets.

rows.name: Toei Subway
rows.cardText: All four lines, all stations (since Dec 23, 2025)
notes: Asakusa, Mita, Shinjuku and Oedo lines.
Toei says that at some gates you need to use the staffed window instead.

rows.name: Nine other Tokyo-area railways
rows.cardText: Odakyu, Odakyu Hakone, Keio, Keikyu, Sotetsu, Seibu, Tokyu, Tobu, Yokohama Minatomirai
notes: Since March 25, 2026, these work together with Tokyo Metro and Toei: 11 railways, 54 lines, 729 stations.
Odakyu Hakone, Seibu and Tobu have some stations where cards don't work. Check before you rely on it.

rows.name: JR East
rows.cardText: No card tap at the gates
notes: You can't tap a credit card at JR East gates, ticket windows or ticket machines.

You can buy tickets by inserting a credit or debit card at a JR ticket office (Midori-no-madoguchi) or a purple reserved-seat machine. Green ticket machines don't take credit cards; black machines take them only for some tickets.
To ride, use a Suica or PASMO, or buy a ticket.
source: JR East FAQ: paying by card (Japanese)

rows.name: Osaka Metro
notes: Adult fare only. Tap the card reader on the gate.
Osaka Metro doesn't say what happens if your train keeps going onto another company's line. Ask staff before riding on.

where.others: Some lines aren't part of this group of 11, including Keisei, the Tokyo Monorail and the Rinkai Line. A few have their own card system (Yurikamome, for example) that doesn't connect with the others. If you're not sure, use your Suica.

example.title: Example: Asakusa → Oshiage → Narita Airport
points: Some Toei Asakusa Line trains keep going past Oshiage onto Keisei tracks, including Access Express trains to Narita Airport.
Your card works on Toei, and you can tap in and out at Oshiage itself.
Keisei isn't one of the 11 card-tap railways, so your card doesn't cover the Keisei part to the airport.
For this trip, use a Suica or PASMO, or buy a Keisei ticket. If you already tapped a card and rode past Oshiage, go to the staffed gate where you get off and show that card.
The Keisei Skyliner doesn't stop at Oshiage. It runs from Keisei Ueno and Nippori to Narita Airport, and all seats are reserved.

why.title: Why your card might not work
items: JR East gates have no credit card reader. At a JR gate you need a Suica, PASMO or ticket. You can buy the ticket with a credit card at a ticket office or a purple machine.
Your train kept going onto another company's line

Many subway trains keep running onto other lines without you changing trains. On Tokyo Metro, if that line is JR East, Saitama Rapid Railway or Toyo Rapid, your card trip doesn't count and you pay in two parts without the card. See the steps above.
That station or gate doesn't take cards
You can't start a Tokyo Metro card trip at Nakano. Toei says some of its gates send you to the staffed window.
You tapped out with something else
You must get in and out with the same card on the same device. A physical card and the same card in Apple Pay count as two different cards.
The credit card reader is a separate pad on the gate, not the spot for Suica and PASMO. Tap the pad with the contactless symbol and wait for the beep.
why.fallback: If none of these fits, go to the staffed gate. Staff can see what the gate recorded.

compare.title: Suica vs credit card vs JR Pass
compare.intro: For getting around a city, a Suica or PASMO card is still the easiest. A credit card is a good backup on the subway. The JR Pass is a separate decision about long JR trips.

cards.name: Suica / PASMO (IC card)
points: Works on JR, Tokyo Metro, Toei and the private railways.
Also works in other cities, alongside cards like ICOCA in Osaka and Kyoto.
PASMO can be added to the Wallet app on an iPhone 8 or later.

cards.name: Contactless credit card
points: Nothing to buy or reload. On Tokyo Metro you pay the same fare as a paper ticket.
Adult fare only. Doesn't work at JR East gates.
Use the same card or phone to get in and out.

cards.name: JR Pass
points: Covers JR trains and the Tokyo Monorail, but not Nozomi or Mizuho bullet trains.
Doesn't cover Tokyo Metro or Toei. Don't buy it for subway rides.
Only worth a look if your trip is built around long JR rides.

subwayTicket.title: Riding the subway all day? Tokyo Subway Ticket
subwayTicket.text: Unlimited Tokyo Metro and Toei rides for 24, 48 or 72 hours: ¥1,000, ¥1,500 or ¥2,000 for adults. For overseas visitors, and Japan residents who live outside Tokyo and seven nearby prefectures. Not valid on JR or Keisei.

faq: Can I use Apple Pay or Google Pay on the Tokyo subway?
Yes, if the phone has an eligible card in its wallet. Tokyo Metro takes phones with Visa, Mastercard, JCB, American Express or Discover. Use the same phone to get in and out.
Can I tap my credit card on the JR Yamanote Line?
No. JR East gates don't take a credit card tap. Use a Suica or PASMO, or buy a ticket.
Can I buy JR tickets with a credit card?

Yes, by inserting the card, not tapping it. JR East ticket offices and purple reserved-seat machines take Visa, Mastercard, JCB, American Express, Diners Club and Discover. Green machines don't take credit cards.
Can I tap a credit card at Shinjuku Station?
At the Tokyo Metro, Toei, Odakyu and Keio gates, yes. At the JR gates, no. Check which company's gate you're walking through.
Which cards does Tokyo Metro accept?
Visa, Mastercard, JCB, American Express, Diners Club, Discover and UnionPay cards with the tap-to-pay symbol: credit, debit or prepaid.
Do kids pay less with a credit card?
No. Card trips are charged the adult fare. Kids should use a child IC card or a child ticket.
Can I take the Narita Express with a credit card tap?
Not by tapping. The Narita Express is a JR East train. Use a Suica, or buy a ticket: JR ticket offices and purple reserved-seat machines take credit cards inserted into the machine.
Can I tap my credit card from Asakusa or Oshiage to Narita Airport?
Not for the whole trip. Trains past Oshiage run on Keisei tracks, and Keisei isn't one of the card-tap railways. Use a Suica or PASMO, or buy a Keisei ticket.
Do I still need a Suica?
If you'll ride any JR line, yes, or buy tickets for those trips. If you only ride the subway, a contactless card can be enough.
Does the JR Pass work on Tokyo Metro?
No. The JR Pass covers JR lines and the Tokyo Monorail. Tokyo Metro and Toei aren't on its list.
